partialCapture.note: Neither the 456-frame sweep nor the 12-theme sweep was regenerated. Frames added or refreshed here were captured against the same guards (assertFramePaints) but only in the two brand themes, and the live-app frames came from the real Electron window rather than Storybook. The spacing round REFRESHED the five chat-tool-rows surfaces because the row pitch changed under them, and added two: `spacing-uniformity` reproduces the three runs the operator screenshotted, `turn-boundary` shows the hierarchy that survives the tightening. `narrow` and `working-labels` are now captured in a viewport sized to their content — at 1280x900 they were mostly empty ground and crossed the uniformity ceiling once the rows tightened. REMEDIATION ROUND 1: all seven chat-tool-rows surfaces were refreshed again, because the name/summary gutter, the running row's live clock, the sr-only outcome text and the summary fallback all changed what they show. REMEDIATION ROUND 2: `real-conversation-tool-rows` was RE-CAPTURED and is no longer stale. It now shows 38 real tool rows with 0 blank object columns on a 20px pitch, rendered by the shipped reducer and the shipped CanonicalTranscript over real /history pages paged oldest-first in 20-entry pages (the cross-page condition the blank-summary defect needed). Electron is not required for this surface — the desktop API answers a plain bearer request. The reading was proven falsifiable by running the SAME harness with the reducer starved: stripping tool_calls alone still yields 0 blanks (the output fallback carries it), stripping tool_calls AND output yields 53 of 53 blank, reproducing the original defect from the current head. DIFF BODY: two surfaces were ADDED — the `write`/`edit` row's expansion now paints the result's own unified diff instead of its arguments JSON — and four frames were taken for them in the two brand palettes (`chat-tool-rows--diff-body` at 1280x2110 and `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow` at 560x1380). The four Storybook frames are committed under `write-edit-diff/` rather than under the story-id directory the capturer derives (`chat-tool-rows/<leaf>`), following the `tool-rows/` precedent, so that the frames sit beside the spec and README that explain them; a re-capture writes them back to `chat-tool-rows/`. `surfaces` counts the two new STORIES entries. The 12-theme sweep was NOT regenerated. A sixth frame set is declared in `supplementary` below: three real durable diff rows in one conversation (197, 58 and 14 diff lines — the first two longer than the 40-line display cap, so two overflow markers and one body shown whole) rendered by the SHIPPED reducer and transcript over real transcript.jsonl rows. The story proves the component; that one proves the wire payload reaches pixels. DIFF BODY, REMEDIATION ROUND 1: the same two Storybook surfaces were refreshed again and a THIRD was added, because the body now paints each line whole in its kind's ink instead of tinting only the leading marker (the terminal's loop is the authority; its docstring promises the other thing), and because the cap's `… N more diff lines` marker is now pinned to the well's foot with `sticky -bottom-3 pb-3 -mb-3` — it used to scroll out of view in exactly the wrapped-at-cap case it exists for. The new surface, `chat-tool-rows--diff-body-narrow-wrapped-cap` at 560x830, is the frame that shows the marker visible at rest; `frames` moves 478 -> 480 for its two palettes, and it is the only frame count that changed. The `real-durable-diff-rows` pair was RE-CAPTURED in the same round for the same reason (on the same real conversation, same three diffs of 197, 58 and 14 lines) and carries the identical marker arithmetic. It was captured from the committed source, not from a dirty tree: this partial run's `head`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` name the commit whose pixels these are. The neighbour `tool-rows/*` frames were NOT re-captured — they are from the August head and do not reproduce pixel-exactly on this one (a uniform 11px shift with identical internal geometry, across three stories of different content), which the write-edit-diff README records so nobody reads it as a regression from this change. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 1: all twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the round changed what they show, not merely how they look. Two of them were the point: `loading` and `fetching` previously photographed states the shipped container could not produce (an ENABLED `Ask providers now` at first paint, when react-query reports isLoading and isFetching together; and cached numbers retained during a live ask, which the query key switch discarded). Both states are now reachable in the app, so both frames are captured from the real behaviour rather than from hand-fed props, and the agreement between story args and container props is pinned by scripts/usage-container.test.mjs rather than by this note. No story was deleted, so `frames` (498) and `surfaces` (57) are unchanged and still equal what is on disk. The other ten were re-captured because the fixes are visible in them: the bar track now carries a `border-control` boundary (measured 1.11:1 -> 2.05:1 against the card on the rendered dark frame, which is what makes a 0% row read as an empty meter and a 100% row as a full one), the unmeasurable window's dotted rule moved off floor-exempt `ink-disabled` onto `ink-dim`, staleness is measured against the set's newest confirmation so `stale-report` again shows one marked block beside one unmarked, prose left monospace, and the tally and the dead-grant note changed wording. `chat-usage--loading`'s capture viewport grew 360 -> 470 so the third skeleton block is not sliced through its own card border. `real-data/` was ALSO re-captured, from the same real backend response replayed through scripts/usage-real-evidence.mjs --payload, because it is the frame two of the fixes were diagnosed from: it read `Cached report, just now.` above blocks dated `1h ago` and showed all eleven blocks degraded. It now reads `Cached report, 34m ago.` and marks 10 of 11 - openrouter, the one account genuinely confirmed at the newest stamp, is unmarked - so the staleness mark distinguishes something again. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 2 (remediation): the same twelve `chat-usage` story surfaces were RE-CAPTURED in both brand themes (24 frames) because the scroll-fold treatment changed what most of them show. The fold rule is no longer an unconditional per-picker prop: it is measured per state from the scroll container, so the six states whose content ends above the fold (`empty`, `query-error`, `fetching`, `percent-only`, `remaining-balance`, `narrow`) no longer draw a boundary under nothing, and the states that do overflow carry a `border-control` rule (3:1 structural floor, pinned at the call site in scripts/contrast-contract.mjs) plus a 20px bottom fade that retracts at the end of the list. `loading` also changed copy: the first paint reads `Reading cached usage` rather than `Asking providers`, because opening the view is a cache read and not a provider ask. No story was added or deleted, so `frames` (498) and `surfaces` (57) are unchanged and still equal what is on disk. `real-data/` was NOT re-captured this round and is STALE with respect to the fold treatment: it still shows the round-1 clip. This machine's backend currently returns zero provider reports, so scripts/usage-real-evidence.mjs cannot re-derive the frame, and no saved `--payload` response from the 11-report run survives in the repository (it is deliberately never committed). The fold fix was instead verified at that exact density in the interaction harness - 11 provider blocks, 22 windows, 1217px of content in a 520px box - measuring a 1px `border-control` rule and a gradient mask at the top of the scroll and the mask retracted with the rule still present at the bottom, in both brand themes. Everything else `real-data` is evidence for (the staleness baseline, the description line, the multi-account keying) is unaffected by this round's changes. USAGE REVIEW ROUND 3: the story `chat-usage--dense` was ADDED (the thirteenth chat-usage surface, 2 frames in the two brand themes), so `frames` (498 -> 500) and `surfaces` (57 -> 58) were corrected by hand per the accounting rule above. It exists because the only committed frame at overflowing density was `real-data/`, which is one commit stale against the fold treatment and cannot be re-derived on demand; `dense` is the same density built from fixtures - eleven reports, twenty-eight windows, five anthropic accounts, the identities and labels the real response shapes - so any sweep can re-take it. The fold it photographs was measured in the same session against the same Storybook build, in both brand themes: 1273px of content in the 520px body cap (753px hidden), a 20px gradient mask plus a 1px `border-control` rule on the wrapper at scrollTop 0, the mask RETRACTED with the rule still present at scrollTop max, and no treatment at all on a fitting state (`percent-only` measured 0px hidden, no mask, 0px border). `real-data/` was NOT re-captured, and this time the live refill was attempted for real: the exact request the button makes (GET /v1/desktop/usage?live=true&refresh=true, authenticated with the running server's own desktop bearer) answered source=live with ZERO reports in ~50ms, and explicit per-provider asks for every usage-capable provider also returned zero - the backend's current credential view has no usage-reportable providers, so its cache cannot be refilled from here. `real-data/` therefore remains stale with respect to the fold treatment, its staleness stays recorded, and the fold at real density is evidenced by `dense`, which is re-derivable.

supplementary.why: The claims are a real pointer hover and a click that stages a draft. Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. The sidebar has no story, so re-running the sweep cannot re-derive them; docs/evidence/sidebar-new-chat/README.md carries the re-capture procedure.

supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).

The only frames in this tree rendered against a REAL /v1/desktop/usage response rather than story fixtures: 11 provider reports and 28 windows as the local backend actually returned them, which is what proves the ported view renders the wire shape and not merely its own fixtures. Storybook cannot produce them (the payload needs the desktop bearer), so the sweep cannot re-derive these two frames. Account identities are redacted shape-preservingly by the capture script; every number, window, tier, unit and staleness value is the backend's own. docs/evidence/chat-usage/README.md carries the re-capture procedure. RE-CAPTURED for review round 1 from the same real response (replayed via `--payload`, since this machine's backend now returns zero reports and cannot re-derive it): the committed pair was the evidence for the staleness-baseline and description defects, so leaving it would have shipped a picture of the bug beside its fix. ROUND 3: a genuine live refill was attempted (live=true&refresh=true with the server's own bearer, plus explicit per-provider asks) and the backend returned zero reports for every provider - its credential view currently has no usage-reportable providers - so these two frames remain one commit stale with respect to the round-2 fold treatment. The fold at this density is evidenced by the re-derivable `chat-usage--dense` story instead.
